Purely conceptual critique or redefinition of a construct with only verbal or illustrative arguments.
Context-bound descriptive findings (one occupation or sector) framed as institutional or contextual nuance rather than a general mechanism.
Lab, online, or vignette experiments on stylized tasks or hypothetical perceptions, when the rival uses field randomization or real behavioral data.
Methodological critique of an existing measure pitched as guidance for 'organizational' or strategy scholars rather than answering a substantive question.

changelog.before: Credible causal identification (policy shocks, sudden events, instruments, randomization) beats panel associations with moderators, even on large samples.
changelog.after: Credible causal identification (random or quasi-random assignment, unexpected deaths or shocks, instruments, policy changes) decisively beats panel associations with moderators, even with richer theory.
changelog.reason: In several low-confidence pairs the identified study won over moderator-heavy panels; the rule needed more decisive weight.

changelog.before: A formal model (real options, matching, game, optimal choice) that derives predictions, especially when tested by field experiment or data, even if magnitudes are unstated.
changelog.after: A formal model (real options, matching, game, optimal choice) deriving predictions tested on field or archival data, ideally several datasets, even if magnitudes are unstated.
changelog.reason: A model tested on multiple archival datasets beat a hand-collected replication study, but the board was unsure.

changelog.before: When both abstracts are sociological, prefer the one testing behavioral outcomes on large archival data over qualitative or multimethod case work.
changelog.after: On sociological or audience-perception topics, prefer large-scale behavioral evidence from archival or platform data over experiments, qualitative, or multimethod case work.
changelog.reason: Platform-data audience study beat an experiment built around a coined paradox; the rule now covers experiments too.

changelog.before: Tests a common management practice (rankings, pay, hiring tools) on firm records, ruling out alternative mechanisms or showing standard remedies fail.
changelog.after: Traces an observed gap to a specific channel by explicitly ruling out competing explanations (selection, signaling, enforcer bias, anticipation).
changelog.reason: Management Science winners decomposed effects and excluded rival channels; generalized beyond management practices.

changelog.before: Contribution framed around named literatures or coined labels (a new 'paradox', a named hypothesis, optimal distinctiveness, categories) rather than a substantive answer.
changelog.after: Contribution is a named literature or coined label (a 'paradox', named hypothesis, optimal distinctiveness) itself, not an identified, tested effect.
changelog.reason: A Management Science winner introduced a new construct but backed it with an instrument; the label alone should not penalize it.

changelog.before: Long verbal theorizing ('we/I theorize', inverted U, lists of moderators) where the data merely confirm predicted directions without identification.
changelog.after: Long verbal theorizing ('we/I theorize', inverted U, moderation by life stage or structure, bridging perspectives) where data merely confirm directions without identification.
changelog.reason: Losers framed contributions as contingent moderation or as bridging scholarly perspectives without identification.

changelog.before: Multimethod designs that combine a case narrative with hypothetical-vignette experiments to illustrate a perception mechanism.
changelog.after: Lab, online, or vignette experiments on stylized tasks or hypothetical perceptions, when the rival uses field randomization or real behavioral data.
changelog.reason: Lab and real-effort experiments lost to field experiments and archival mechanism studies in multiple pairs.
